record.paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
record.original_question: For the delayed p-periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) - h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic nonnegative harvesting sequence, investigate the global dynamics: characterize persistence and extinction, the structure of any persistent set, boundedness and strong persistence of persistent solutions, periodic attractors or other limiting behavior, and how these properties depend on the sequence h_0, h_1, ..., h_{p-1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous function (typically a contest-competition-type per-capita growth function, e.g. continuous, positive, and decreasing with $\lim_{x\to\infty} x f(x) < \infty$). Fix an integer $p\ge 1$ and let $(h_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative real numbers (so $h_{n+p}=h_n$ for all $n\ge 0$). Consider the second-order delayed difference equation with periodic harvesting
$$ x_{n+1} \;=\; x_n\, f(x_{n-1}) \;-\; h_n, \qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots, $$
with nonnegative initial data $x_{-1},x_0\ge 0$, where the iteration is considered only as long as the right-hand side remains nonnegative (otherwise the population is declared extinct).

Carry out a complete global analysis of this equation. Specifically:

(a) Characterize, in terms of the harvesting vector $(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_{p-1})$ and the function $f$, the set of initial conditions $(x_{-1},x_0)$ that lead to extinction (the orbit becomes nonpositive in finite time) versus those that persist (remain strictly positive for all $n$).

(b) Describe the structure (topological and dynamical) of the persistent set: is it open, connected, bounded, invariant?

(c) Show whether every persistent solution is bounded and strongly persistent, i.e. $0<\liminf_{n\to\infty} x_n \le \limsup_{n\to\infty} x_n <\infty$, and identify sharp conditions on $(h_0,\ldots,h_{p-1})$ ensuring this.

(d) Determine the limiting behavior of persistent solutions: existence, multiplicity, and global attractivity of $p$-periodic (or $2p$-periodic) solutions, and/or the occurrence of more complex attractors.

(e) Describe how the answers in (a)–(d) depend on the harvesting profile $(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_{p-1})$, including monotonicity in each $h_i$ and bifurcations as the harvesting amplitudes vary.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals only partial results: studies of $x_{n+1}=x_n f(x_{n-1})$ under constant-yield harvesting establish some stability, boundedness and persistence facts, and related delayed harvesting models exhibit complex dynamics (period doubling, chaos). No source provides a full global characterization for general $p$-periodic harvesting in the delayed contest-competition model, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The dynamics of some discrete models with delay under the effect of constant yield harvesting
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the dynamics of population models of the form x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) under constant yield harvesting, providing results on stability, boundedness, persistence and oscillations.
status_evidence.claim: Only the constant-harvesting (non-periodic) version has been analyzed, leaving the periodic case open.

status_evidence.title: On persistence of a Nicholson-type system with multiple delays and nonlinear harvesting
status_evidence.snippet: Considers models with multiple delays and nonlinear harvesting, obtaining sufficient conditions for strong and uniform persistence.
status_evidence.claim: Persistence is established only under specific structural hypotheses, not as a general characterization for periodic harvesting.

status_evidence.title: Time-Delay Dynamics in Fishery Resources under Periodic Harvesting
status_evidence.snippet: Presents periodic fisheries management models incorporating delayed decision effects, with numerics showing quasi-periodicity, period-doubling and chaos.
status_evidence.claim: Complex dynamics are documented numerically, indicating no complete analytic global theory yet.
